questions.title: Factory: replace a transaction type without editing the existing agent or sequences
questions.prompt:
An existing `packet` class has 8-bit `src_id` and `dst_id` fields and a 16-bit `payload`. The agent and sequences must **not** be modified.

Write `priority_packet`, which extends `packet` and adds a random 2-bit priority:
- when `dst_id == 8'hFF` (broadcast) the priority must be non-zero;
- unicast packets are unrestricted.

At runtime, use the UVM factory to replace every `packet` with a `priority_packet`.
questions.answer:
- Extend the class; existing code keeps referring to `packet` and the factory returns the subclass at create time.
- `priority` is a reserved SV keyword, so name the field `pri`. It is 2 bits wide, so no range constraint is needed.
- Use an implication `(dst_id == 8'hFF) -> (pri != 0)`; an unconditional `pri != 0` would wrongly restrict unicast.
- Register the override **before** `super.build_phase()` (before anything is created). `new()` bypasses the factory; only `type_id::create()` honors overrides.
- Per-agent replacement: `set_inst_override_by_type(orig, repl, path)`; the path must match `get_full_name()`.
- To read `pri` in a scoreboard, `$cast` to `priority_packet` first.
questions.solution:
**Key idea:** subclass `packet`, register it with `` `uvm_object_utils ``, and install a factory type override *before* anything calls `packet::type_id::create()`. Old sequences still ask for a `packet`; the factory quietly hands them a `priority_packet`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant T as my_test
  participant F as uvm_factory
  participant S as old_sequence
  T->>F: set_type_override_by_type(packet, priority_packet)
  T->>T: super.build_phase() builds env and agents
  S->>F: packet::type_id::create(pkt)
  F-->>S: priority_packet object behind a packet handle
  S->>S: randomize() also solves c_pri
```

### Solution
- **Extend, don't edit.** `priority_packet extends packet` inherits `src_id`, `dst_id`, `payload` (never redeclare them, that would shadow the parent fields).
- **Field name:** `priority` is a reserved keyword (`priority case/if`), so use `pri`. A 2-bit field is already bounded to 0..3.
- **Constraint:** an implication so only broadcast is restricted.
- **Override timing:** `build_phase` runs top-down, so in the test put the override *before* `super.build_phase()` (the base test's build creates the env, and sequences create items later in `run_phase`).

| Override API | Scope | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_type_override_by_type(packet::get_type(), priority_packet::get_type())` | every `packet` created anywhere | swap the whole TB |
| `set_inst_override_by_type(packet::get_type(), priority_packet::get_type(), "uvm_test_top.env.agt0.*")` | only matching `get_full_name()` paths | one agent only |
| `packet::type_id::set_type_override(priority_packet::get_type())` | same as the first row | shorthand from the class |

### Code
```systemverilog
class priority_packet extends packet;
  `uvm_object_utils(priority_packet)

  rand bit [1:0] pri;            // "priority" is a reserved keyword

  // Broadcast must carry a non-zero priority; unicast is unrestricted
  constraint c_pri { (dst_id == 8'hFF) -> (pri != 0); }

  function new(string name = "priority_packet");
    super.new(name);
  endfunction
endclass

class prio_test extends base_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(prio_test)

  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
  endfunction

  function void build_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    // original type first, replacement second
    set_type_override_by_type(packet::get_type(), priority_packet::get_type());
    super.build_phase(phase);    // base_test creates the env here
  endfunction
endclass

// Reading pri in a scoreboard
function void write(packet p);
  priority_packet pp;
  if (!$cast(pp, p))
    `uvm_error("SB", "got a plain packet: override not applied")
  else
    `uvm_info("SB", $sformatf("dst=%0h pri=%0d", pp.dst_id, pp.pri), UVM_HIGH)
endfunction
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- **Swapped arguments** mean "replace `priority_packet` with `packet`": the override appears to be set but has no effect.
- **`new()` instead of `type_id::create()`** anywhere in the old code bypasses the factory. An object that already exists never changes type.
- **Override registered too late** (e.g. in `run_phase` or inside a sequence's `body()` after items were created).
- **Instance override path** must match the *creating context's* full name; check with `factory.print()` / `uvm_top.print_topology()`.

### Follow-ups
- **Why not register the override inside a sequence's `body()`?** Items are created as soon as `body()` runs, so it arrives too late (and it is global anyway).
- **The override is registered but objects are still the base class.** The code calls `new()` instead of `type_id::create()`.
- **Scope of a type override?** Global: every `packet::type_id::create()` returns the subclass.
- **An instance override has no effect.** The path doesn't match the target's `get_full_name()`.

questions.title: Scoreboard: align the golden model with a 1-cycle-latency MAC
questions.prompt:
A streaming MAC takes signed `a[7:0]`, `b[7:0]` and `acc_in[15:0]` every cycle and produces

`acc_out = a*b + acc_in` **one cycle later**.

Write a UVM scoreboard that computes the expected value in `write()`, compares it with the DUT output, and reports `uvm_error` on a mismatch. Each monitor transaction carries this cycle's inputs and this cycle's `acc_out` pin value.
questions.answer:
- `a`, `b`, `acc_in` are random; `acc_out` is an observed output and must not be `rand`.
- Push each prediction into a queue; pop the oldest only once the queue holds more than one entry (cycle 0 has nothing to compare).
- Widen before multiplying: `16'(tr.a) * 16'(tr.b)`; otherwise the product is computed in 8 bits.
- Compare with `!==` so an X on the DUT output is a mismatch.
- Connect `mon.ap.connect(sb.imp)` in connect_phase. For latency N, pop when size > N. Don't name a variable `ref` (keyword).

questions.title: Parameterized interface: write stream_if with clocking blocks and driver/monitor modports
questions.prompt: Write `stream_if` with a parameter `N` (4, 8 or 16). It carries `N` signed 8-bit data values plus a `valid` signal. Provide clocking blocks and separate **driver** and **monitor** modports. `clk` and `rst_n` are interface ports.
questions.answer:
- Data is an unpacked array `logic signed [7:0] data[N]`, not one packed bus.
- Driver and monitor see opposite directions: one clocking block each.
- `input #1step` samples just before the edge; a small positive output skew (`#1`) drives just after it, so the DUT never sees the change on the same edge.
- Type the virtual interface with its modport (`virtual stream_if#(4).drv`); driving signals directly bypasses the clocking block.
- `stream_if#(4)` and `stream_if#(8)` are different types; config_db won't convert.

questions.title: Virtual sequence: run a command stream and a data stream in parallel
questions.prompt:
The command and data interfaces each have their own sequencer (`cmd_sequencer`, `data_sequencer`). Write:
1. a **virtual sequencer** that holds both handles,
2. a **layered sequence** that runs a command sequence and a data sequence in parallel,
3. the test `run_phase` that starts it.
questions.answer:
- The virtual sequencer only holds handles: it generates no items and must not construct the lower sequencers. Assign the handles in the env's connect_phase.
- A sequence uses `` `uvm_object_utils ``; `` `uvm_declare_p_sequencer `` gives a typed `p_sequencer`, valid only after `seq.start(env.vseqr)`.
- Start each child inside `fork ... join` so both run and both finish.
- Raise/drop an objection around `start` in run_phase.
- Never start both children on the same sequencer (serialized onto one channel).

questions.title: Constraints plus cross coverage for a memory transaction
questions.prompt:
`mem_txn` has `addr[7:0]`, `access_type` (READ or WRITE) and `burst_len` from 1 to 8. A WRITE burst may only be 1, 4 or 8.

Write the constraints, a covergroup that covers all three fields and **crosses `access_type` with `burst_len`**, plus a `sample()` method.
questions.answer:
- Constrain `burst_len inside {[1:8]}` first, then `(access_type == WRITE) -> burst_len inside {1,4,8}`; the implication alone leaves READ unbounded (`int` can go to 0 or negative).
- Construct the covergroup in `new()`. `randomize()` doesn't sample: call `sample()` after a successful randomize, before the driver touches the item.
- WRITE x {2,3,5,6,7} cross cells stay at zero by design: exclude them with `ignore_bins`; `illegal_bins` only fire if something bypasses the constraint.
- Don't create 256 address bins; two ranges are enough.

questions.title: AXI read scoreboard: flag an RID that has no matching ARID
questions.prompt:
A response with `rid = 2` appears on the AXI R channel, but no read with `arid = 2` was ever issued.

Write a scoreboard that tracks outstanding reads (reported by a monitor on each AR handshake and on each R burst completion), raises `uvm_error` on an unmatched response, and retires the ID once it is matched.
questions.answer:
- Track each ID with an `int` counter in an associative array, not a 1-bit flag: one ID can have several reads outstanding.
- Increment on each AR handshake (`arvalid && arready`). On R, error if the ID is absent or zero; else decrement and delete when it reaches zero.
- Both imps carry `bit [7:0]`, so use `` `uvm_analysis_imp_decl(_arid) `` / `(_rid)` outside the class for distinct `write_arid`/`write_rid`.
- Retire once per burst, on the `rlast` beat. Sample only on `valid && ready`.
- In report_phase, report IDs still outstanding (AR with no response).
questions.solution:
**Key idea:** an AR handshake *opens* a read for its ID, an R burst (its `rlast` beat) *closes* one. Keep a **per-ID counter** (`int outstanding[bit [7:0]]`); an R whose ID has count 0 is exactly the protocol error.

```wavedrom
{ "signal": [
  { "name": "clk",     "wave": "p......." },
  { "name": "arvalid", "wave": "01.0...." },
  { "name": "arready", "wave": "01.0...." },
  { "name": "arid",    "wave": "x==x....", "data": ["1", "1"] },
  {},
  { "name": "rvalid",  "wave": "0001..0." },
  { "name": "rready",  "wave": "0001..0." },
  { "name": "rid",     "wave": "xxx===x.", "data": ["1", "1", "2"] },
  { "name": "rlast",   "wave": "0001..0." }
],
  "head": { "text": "two reads with ARID 1 are matched; RID 2 at cycle 5 has no ARID" } }
```

| Cycle | event | `outstanding` after | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | AR id=1 | {1:1} | |
| 2 | AR id=1 | {1:2} | a 1-bit flag would lose this |
| 3 | R id=1, rlast | {1:1} | matched |
| 4 | R id=1, rlast | {} (entry deleted) | matched |
| 5 | R id=2, rlast | {} | **uvm_error: RID 2 has no ARID** |

### Solution
- Two analysis imps with the same payload type need `` `uvm_analysis_imp_decl `` to generate distinct classes and `write_*` methods.
- The monitor sends `arid` on every AR handshake and `rid` once per burst (beat with `rlast`), never on idle or stalled cycles.
- Decrementing on every beat would make the second beat of a burst look unmatched.

### Code
```systemverilog
`uvm_analysis_imp_decl(_arid)
`uvm_analysis_imp_decl(_rid)

class axi_id_sb extends uvm_scoreboard;
  `uvm_component_utils(axi_id_sb)

  uvm_analysis_imp_arid #(bit [7:0], axi_id_sb) arid_imp;
  uvm_analysis_imp_rid  #(bit [7:0], axi_id_sb) rid_imp;
  int outstanding[bit [7:0]];          // key width = ARID/RID width

  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
    arid_imp = new("arid_imp", this);
    rid_imp  = new("rid_imp",  this);
  endfunction

  // AR handshake (arvalid && arready)
  function void write_arid(bit [7:0] id);
    outstanding[id]++;                 // missing key starts at 0
  endfunction

  // Called once per burst, on the rlast beat (rvalid && rready && rlast)
  function void write_rid(bit [7:0] id);
    if (!outstanding.exists(id) || outstanding[id] == 0)
      `uvm_error("AXI_ID", $sformatf("RID %0d has no matching ARID", id))
    else begin
      outstanding[id]--;
      if (outstanding[id] == 0) outstanding.delete(id);
    end
  endfunction

  function void report_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    foreach (outstanding[id])
      `uvm_error("AXI_ID", $sformatf("ARID %0d: %0d read(s) never answered", id, outstanding[id]))
  endfunction
endclass
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- Key narrower than the ID truncates upper bits: different IDs collide in one entry.
- `outstanding.delete(id)` (parentheses); `delete[id]` is a syntax error.
- With multiple masters behind an interconnect, key on `{master, id}`.

### Follow-ups
- **Catch an AR that never gets a response?** Report every ID still in `outstanding` in report_phase (or a timeout per entry).
- **Also check data ordering?** Store a queue of expected data per ID: AXI keeps order *within* an ID, not across IDs.
- **SVA alternative?** A local-variable property `(arvalid && arready, id = arid) |-> ##[1:N] (rvalid && rid == id)`, but counting outstanding reads belongs in the scoreboard.

questions.title: One agent class, multiple interfaces: configure active/passive and vif per instance
questions.prompt: Several identical stream ports exist. `agent0` drives its port; `agent1` only monitors. Write the agent class **once** and use `uvm_config_db` to give each instance its virtual interface and its active/passive mode.
questions.answer:
- The `set` context + path must resolve to the agent's full name: tb sets `"uvm_test_top.env.agent0"` with `null` context, agent calls `get(this, "", ...)`.
- `get` type must match `set` type exactly, modport included. A mismatched field name makes `get` fail: `uvm_fatal` with `get_full_name()`.
- Active agent builds driver + sequencer + monitor; passive only monitor. `is_active` defaults to `UVM_ACTIVE`.
- Don't hard-code "I am agent0" in the class; put differences in configuration. `set(null, "*", ...)` would give every agent the same vif.

questions.title: Register sequence: write CTRL, poll STATUS until ready, then send data
questions.prompt:
Write a sequence that:
1. writes `ctrl_value` to CTRL (address `0x0`),
2. reads STATUS (address `0x4`) until bit 0 is 1 (bound the polling),
3. writes `32'hDEAD_BEEF` to address `0x8`.

Use `start_item` / `randomize` / `finish_item`. The item `reg_seq_item` has `addr`, `data`, `read_write` (0 = write, 1 = read).
questions.answer:
- Extend `uvm_sequence #(reg_seq_item)`; create a fresh item for every transfer.
- Order: `start_item`, constrained `randomize() with {...}`, `finish_item`.
- Read data is valid only after `finish_item` returns (the driver fills it in).
- `do-while` so STATUS is read before bit 0 is checked; after 100 polls, `uvm_error` and `return` (never `$finish` in a sequence).
- If `randomize()` fails, stop; don't send an unrandomized item. The test raises the objection around `seq.start`.

questions.title: fork-join: configure two blocks in parallel, then start datapath traffic
questions.prompt:
Block A and Block B each need **five control registers** written, and both configurations should run **at the same time**. The datapath must start only **after both are done**. The virtual sequencer has `seqr_a`, `seqr_b` and `seqr_dp`.

Write the configuration sequence and the top virtual sequence.
questions.answer:
- One sequence class parameterized by `base_addr` (`32'h1000` for A, `32'h2000` for B); writes go to `base_addr + i*4`, `i = 0..4`.
- Use `fork ... join`: `join_none` doesn't wait, `join_any` waits only for the faster block.
- A and B are two separate objects on two separate sequencers; the datapath sequence starts after the `join` on `seqr_dp`.
- `foreach (int i[5])` is not legal syntax; you start sequence objects, not `seqr_a.start()`.

questions.title: RTL: 4-bit counter that counts only on an enabled, completed valid/ready handshake
questions.prompt:
Design a 4-bit synchronous counter.

- Inputs: `clk`, `reset`, `enable`, `valid`, `ready`. Output: `count[3:0]`.
- `reset` is **active-high and synchronous**.
- The counter increments only when `enable`, `valid` and `ready` are **all 1 in the same cycle**, and wraps from 15 to 0.
questions.answer:
- `always_ff @(posedge clk)`; don't put `reset` in the sensitivity list (that makes it asynchronous).
- Check `reset` first so reset and increment are mutually exclusive; nonblocking `<=`.
- 4-bit `count + 1` wraps from 15 to 0 naturally.
- The TB reference count must wrap at 4 bits too; the monitor samples after the edge settles.
questions.solution:
**Key idea:** a completed handshake is `valid && ready`; gate it with `enable`, give `reset` priority in a single `if / else if`, and let the 4-bit width provide the wrap.

```wavedrom
{ "signal": [
  { "name": "clk",    "wave": "p........." },
  { "name": "reset",  "wave": "1.0......." },
  { "name": "enable", "wave": "0.1....0.." },
  { "name": "valid",  "wave": "0.1.01...0" },
  { "name": "ready",  "wave": "0.101....." },
  { "name": "count",  "wave": "=..=..==..", "data": ["0", "1", "2", "3"] }
],
  "head": { "text": "count increments after cycles 2, 5, 6 only; valid without ready or with enable low does not count" } }
```

| Cycle | enable | valid | ready | count next |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | +1 |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | 0 | hold (stalled) |
| 4 | 1 | 0 | 1 | hold (no data) |
| 7 | 0 | 1 | 1 | hold (disabled) |
| any with count=15 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 (wrap) |

### Code
```systemverilog
module perf_counter (
  input  logic       clk,
  input  logic       reset,      // active-high, synchronous
  input  logic       enable,
  input  logic       valid,
  input  logic       ready,
  output logic [3:0] count
);
  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset)
      count <= '0;
    else if (enable && valid && ready)
      count <= count + 4'd1;     // 4'hF + 1 wraps to 4'h0
  end
endmodule
```

Matching reference model in the TB:
```systemverilog
bit [3:0] ref_cnt;               // 4 bits, so it wraps like the DUT
always @(posedge clk)
  if (reset) ref_cnt <= 0;
  else if (enable && valid && ready) ref_cnt <= ref_cnt + 1;
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- Two separate `if` statements (reset, then increment) let the increment override the reset.
- `@(posedge clk or posedge reset)` makes the reset asynchronous: contradicts the spec.
- A blocking `=` in `always_ff` makes other blocks reading `count` order-dependent.
- An `int` reference count diverges from the DUT at 16.

### Follow-ups
- **Is `count == 15 ? 0 : count + 1` needed?** No: same result as the natural 4-bit wrap.
- **Saturate instead of wrap?** `else if (fire && count != 4'hF) count <= count + 1;`
- **Assertion?** `assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (reset) !(enable && valid && ready) |=> $stable(count));`

questions.title: RTL: 8-input fixed-priority encoder with valid (no X, no latch)
questions.prompt:
Input `irq_req[7:0]`, bit 7 is the **highest** priority.

- `irq_id[2:0]` = index of the highest set bit; `valid` = 1 when any request is set.
- With several requests set, report only the highest.
- With no requests, outputs must not be X and must not infer a latch.
questions.answer:
- `always_comb` with `valid = |irq_req` and a default `irq_id = 0` at the top.
- `priority casez` from bit 7 down, `?` only in lower undecided bits; items overlap on purpose, so not `unique`.
- `8'b0100_1000` gives 6, not 3. Avoid `casex` (hides X on inputs).
- The scoreboard reference model must also scan from high to low.
questions.solution:
**Key idea:** scan from bit 7 down and stop at the first 1. `priority casez` with don't-care `?` in the lower bits does exactly that; a default assignment at the top of `always_comb` guarantees no latch and no X when nothing is requested.

| irq_req | irq_id | valid | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0000_0000` | 0 | 0 | default, no latch |
| `0000_0001` | 0 | 1 | only bit 0 |
| `0100_1000` | **6** | 1 | bit 6 beats bit 3 |
| `1111_1111` | 7 | 1 | bit 7 always wins |
| `0001_0110` | 4 | 1 | |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R["irq_req[7:0]"] --> B7{"bit7?"}
  B7 -->|1| I7["id=7"]
  B7 -->|0| B6{"bit6?"}
  B6 -->|1| I6["id=6"]
  B6 -->|0| DOTS["... bit0?"]
  DOTS -->|1| I0["id=0"]
  DOTS -->|0| DEF["id=0, valid=0"]
```

### Code
```systemverilog
module priority_encoder (
  input  logic [7:0] irq_req,
  output logic [2:0] irq_id,
  output logic       valid
);
  always_comb begin
    valid  = |irq_req;               // reduction OR
    irq_id = 3'd0;                   // default: no latch, no X
    priority casez (irq_req)
      8'b1???_????: irq_id = 3'd7;
      8'b01??_????: irq_id = 3'd6;
      8'b001?_????: irq_id = 3'd5;
      8'b0001_????: irq_id = 3'd4;
      8'b0000_1???: irq_id = 3'd3;
      8'b0000_01??: irq_id = 3'd2;
      8'b0000_001?: irq_id = 3'd1;
      8'b0000_0001: irq_id = 3'd0;
      default:      irq_id = 3'd0;
    endcase
  end
endmodule
```

Loop form (scales to any width):
```systemverilog
always_comb begin
  irq_id = '0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++)        // later (higher) i overwrites earlier
    if (irq_req[i]) irq_id = i[2:0];
end
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- Reversing the case order matches a lower priority first.
- `unique casez` would be wrong: the items overlap by design.
- `casex` treats X on the *input* as don't-care and hides X propagation in simulation.
- A reference model scanning from the LSB mismatches on every multi-request test.

### Follow-ups
- **Is `always comb` valid?** No, syntax error (`always_comb`).
- **If-else chain instead?** Fine, scanning from bit 7 down, but the final `else` must assign both outputs or a latch is inferred.
- **Round-robin instead of fixed priority?** Rotate the request vector by the last grant + 1, fixed-priority encode, rotate back.
- **Where does the reference logic live?** In the scoreboard; the monitor only samples and forwards.
